steps.content: An unfamiliar ceiling, the edge of an unfamiliar bed, and unfamiliar curtains.
And...
An unfamiliar person.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: How are you recovering? Chief?

options: I guess I just got burns.
I thought I was gonna die.

choices.text: I guess I just got burns.
I thought I was gonna die.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Thanks to my perfect control of firepower.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: I was trying really hard to control the firepower!

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Blame it on Laplace, he was the one who went too far.
I still think the person who locked me in a metal can was the one who went too far.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: No clue. All the surveillance equipment has been destroyed by fire.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: And I didn't find any trace of him.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Ugh... I was so sure I would succeed the first time! If he hadn't held me back, I probably could have done it!

options: Can you give me a heads-up next time?

choices.text: Can you give me a heads-up next time?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Uh... nope.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Why?!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I almost died in that experiment.

options: What happened to that thing inside me?

choices.text: What happened to that thing inside me?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: While you were asleep, I did a complete and comprehensive physical examination on you.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Eh... What's that expression supposed to mean?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Come on, it was handled by the drones—of course I didn't touch you or anything.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And what's the final conclusion?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: There's good news and bad news. Which one do you want to hear first?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: I strongly recommend you start with the good news.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Your body is in good condition, Chief!
And what's the bad news?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: The bad news is that... um, that thing still exists inside your body.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: If you overuse the shackles or get too close to a Black Ring... I can't guarantee what will end up happening.

options: So just the same as before.

choices.text: So just the same as before.

steps.content: You chuckle drily, thinking of it as running a lap... then returning to the starting point.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: I was wondering, Chief... if I apologize to you solemnly, can you pretend what happened today was just a dream?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Everything is just as it was before. Nothing happened. Don't look into anything. There are certain things that can put you in great danger the more you know about them.
At least for now, your body apparently hasn't gone through any actual abnormal changes.
But you must make Summer go into the confinement cell, and she won't be allowed to have chocolate for a while. She'd better be prepared to face the consequences of doing such a thing to the Chief.
You look down at the unfamiliar hospital bed and suddenly recall something very important.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Ah...

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Let's wait a bit longer.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This is a kidnap case aimed at the Chief, Sinner Summer.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If we go back too late, your punishment won't be as simple as going into the confinement cell.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Well, then... At least wait till after we finish watching the ending of The Age of Youth.
Summer begins blinking excessively at you.
Usually, when she does that, it means she's up to something.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Where are we going to watch it?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Downstairs, of course.
Loud noise can be heard from the hallway. Apparently, this is no desolate place.

options: Why isn't there a new videotape for The Age of Youth this time?

choices.text: Why isn't there a new videotape for The Age of Youth this time?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Did Laplace give it to you beforehand?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: No.
Summer shakes her head and motions you to look out the window.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: We're going to shoot it real-time this time!
Just as you're still wondering how Summer, who's very weak physically, carried you upstairs, Summer has already changed into a new outfit.
She's taken off her jacket from the Research Institute and changed into a suit, a small flower clipped to her chest.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: The graduation ceremony is about to begin. Shall we go together, Chief?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: That's the third episode of The Age of Youth—Graduation.
The two of you walk to the playground with all the other students.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Chief! Here, here!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm not wearing a school uniform, what if the security guards notice me and kick me out?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Haha, no worries. I'll tell them you're my parent.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: After all, this is the last day at school. Even the strictest security guard... will surely grant the students' wishes.

options: Why did you decide to come here all of a sudden?

choices.text: Why did you decide to come here all of a sudden?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Because I still don't have the important life experience of graduation.
You almost can't believe your ears.
No graduation? Then how did you get into the Ring Research Institute?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Like... they just asked me.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: They asked me if I wanted to do research on things related to the Ring substance.
And you said yes just like that?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Of course, that's the Ring substance we're talking about! Although it didn't end up well between me and them...
You're suddenly speechless. Apparently, a genius's world is indeed different than that of ordinary people.

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: Testing... Testing...?

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: Can you hear me?
On the makeshift podium, someone who looks like the principal is testing the mic. Once he shows up, the noisy students soon all stop talking.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: I guess... it's beginning now.

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: Eileen!

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: Present!

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: This is for you. I hope that in the future... you will still think of your schoolmates and all your teachers here.

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: You've finished your journey here. But soon enough, you will set off on a new journey.

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: You had good academic achievements and diverse hobbies. If you keep working hard and always apply your thinking... you will certainly find a path best suited for yourself.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: Thank you... Thank you, Principal!
The girl receives her graduation certificate, looking both overjoyed and sentimental.

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: Next... Ronnie!
The boy named Ronnie walks up to the podium steadily.

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: I remember when you first came, you were the most mischievous boy here. It seems like... time really does change a person.

steps.speaker: Ronnie
steps.content: No, it's all because of your guidance.

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: Hahaha... You've even grown to become a smooth talker too! Here, for you! Those who can adapt to the surrounding environment will always be the winners.

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: I'm looking forward to your future achievements, Ronnie!
The students go up the podium one after another, receiving the proof of their three years of study.
The summer wind in June is hot. Even though it's almost evening now, the setting sun is still radiating warmth.
The two of you are standing at the front of the procession. Listening to the principal's graduation speech, Summer suddenly grows sentimental.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Well, to be honest with you, I envy these kids a lot.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: They have healthy bodies, unlike me who's always been sickly... I couldn't do anything on my own. All I could do was sit in the classroom and work on questions.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: It was bearable at first, when my classmates could still talk to me about the questions I was working on. But as I moved on to tougher and tougher questions, everyone in my class treated me like a weirdo.
At the time, you didn't have... any friends in your class?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Hmm... I guess you can say I had one.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And who's that?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Anime.

options: It has to be a person.

choices.text: It has to be a person.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Then... I didn't have any, indeed. But... back then, anime was my only friend.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: That invincible high school girl is everything I long for. She has her youth, her adventures, her friends, and her wonderful daily life. She's given me my infinite imagination and courage.

options: Perhaps that's the price of being a genius.

choices.text: Perhaps that's the price of being a genius.

steps.content: No one truly understands them.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: That's why the ending of The Age of Youth must be like this: having saved the world, the genius high school girl returns to her friends and has her graduation, putting a perfect full stop on her hero adventure.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: But... even if she comes back to school, she has no friends here, so she'll make do with the Chief.
While you are discussing the ending of the third episode, the names of all graduates have already been called.
The students there are all leaving to take pictures with their graduate certificates. Only you and Summer are left in the ceremony venue.
Summer seems a little hesitant, so you propose the idea to her.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Hmm... I guess we can, but let me put on my glasses! What do you think? Do I look more like a high schooler like this?
But just as you want to step into the crowd, you receive a call from Nightingale.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, how are you doing?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I got injured, but it's nothing serious.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Is the Sinner Summer still under your control?
Summer glances at you, a little uneasy.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The MBCC's search unit will arrive at your location right away, please stay where you are.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Copy that.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Sigh... In the end, this is not a ceremony a Sinner can attend.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm sorry.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Hahaha... No need to apologize for something like this, Chief.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: I simply find it interesting. I want to experience things I've never experienced before.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: If something is interesting enough, I'll do it. But the situation this time is special, I'll let it be...

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: This is the way I, Summer, do things in my life.
The graduation ceremony at dusk has come to a perfect end, and you get in the car going back to the Bureau.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Come to think of it, what happened today can only count as a drill.

options: How intense are the regular fights?

choices.text: How intense are the regular fights?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: The crisis threatening the world is even bigger than I thought.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: During the battle with Laplace, I felt a strange power.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: I was lucky to have you by my side, Chief, so I was able to completely offset his power. That's why... you're my necessary catalyst for saving the world.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Ah... No, companion.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: So, let's go back. Go back to the MBCC.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: I don't need help from those deceitful people at the Ring Research Institute.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: No matter what challenges I face, I have to write my own story, find the truth, and save the world in my own way.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Write the perfect ending for The Age of Youth.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Why aren't we allowed to bring anything into the confinement cell, Chief?

options: What kind of confinement cell will that be?

choices.text: What kind of confinement cell will that be?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: But... I want to eat chocolate.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Don't even mention your chocolate.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Do you still remember what happened last time?

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Ahem! That was an accident! An accident!

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: As I've said, invention always involves accidents!

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: ...Ugh, I can at least order some at the Supply Office, can't I?
You can, but you'll need my final approval.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: Sob... Damn it, I can't ask Nightingale to tweak the quantity for me this time.

steps.speaker: Summer
steps.content: If it causes delays in my invention, I won't be able to meet the standards in The Age of Youth, which means I can't save the world. You'll be liable for that! Hey! Don't you run away!
Teary-eyed, the genius inventor watches you leave the confinement cell.
But eventually, in the approval form for the chocolate purchase order, you increase the volume discreetly...
Perhaps this can somewhat compensate the girl for not being able to have her graduation this summer.
